11 /-!
12 # Finite dimension of vector spaces
13 
14 Definition of the rank of a module, or dimension of a vector space, as a natural number.
15 
16 ## Main definitions
17 
18 Defined is `Module.finrank`, the dimension of a finite-dimensional space, returning a
19 `Nat`, as opposed to `Module.rank`, which returns a `Cardinal`. When the space has infinite
20 dimension, its `finrank` is by convention set to `0`.
21 
22 The definition of `finrank` does not assume a `FiniteDimensional` instance, but lemmas might.
23 Import `LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional` to get access to these additional lemmas.
24 
25 Formulas for the dimension are given for linear equivs, in `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq`.
26 
27 ## Implementation notes
28 
29 Most results are deduced from the corresponding results for the general dimension (as a cardinal),
30 in `Dimension.lean`. Not all results have been ported yet.
31 
32 You should not assume that there has been any effort to state lemmas as generally as possible.
33 -/

45 namespace Module

47 section Semiring
48 
49 /-- The rank of a module as a natural number.
50 
51 For a finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `k`, `Module.finrank k V` is equal to
52 the dimension of `V` over `k`.
53 
54 For a general module `M` over a ring `R`, `Module.finrank R M` is defined to be the supremum of the
55 cardinalities of the `R`-linearly independent subsets of `M`, if this supremum is finite. It is
56 defined by convention to be `0` if this supremum is infinite. See `Module.rank` for a
57 cardinal-valued version where infinite rank modules have rank an infinite cardinal.
58 
59 Note that if `R` is not a field then there can exist modules `M` with `¬(Module.Finite R M)` but
60 `finrank R M ≠ 0`. For example `ℚ` has `finrank` equal to `1` over `ℤ`, because the nonempty
61 `ℤ`-linearly independent subsets of `ℚ` are precisely the nonzero singletons. -/
62 noncomputable def finrank (R M : Type*) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] : ℕ :=
63   Cardinal.toNat (Module.rank R M)
64 
65 @[simp] theorem finrank_subsingleton [Subsingleton R] : finrank R M = 1 := by
66   rw [finrank, rank_subsingleton, map_one]
67 
68 theorem finrank_eq_of_rank_eq {n : ℕ} (h : Module.rank R M = ↑n) : finrank R M = n := by
69   simp [finrank, h]
70 
71 lemma rank_eq_one_iff_finrank_eq_one : Module.rank R M = 1 ↔ finrank R M = 1 :=
72   Cardinal.toNat_eq_one.symm
73 
74 /-- This is like `rank_eq_one_iff_finrank_eq_one` but works for `2`, `3`, `4`, ... -/
75 lemma rank_eq_ofNat_iff_finrank_eq_ofNat (n : ℕ) [Nat.AtLeastTwo n] :
76     Module.rank R M = OfNat.ofNat n ↔ finrank R M = OfNat.ofNat n :=
77   Cardinal.toNat_eq_ofNat.symm
78 
79 theorem finrank_le_of_rank_le {n : ℕ} (h : Module.rank R M ≤ ↑n) : finrank R M ≤ n := by
80   rwa [← Cardinal.toNat_le_iff_le_of_lt_aleph0, toNat_natCast] at h
81   · exact h.trans_lt natCast_lt_aleph0
82   · exact natCast_lt_aleph0
83 
84 theorem finrank_lt_of_rank_lt {n : ℕ} (h : Module.rank R M < ↑n) : finrank R M < n := by
85   rwa [← Cardinal.toNat_lt_iff_lt_of_lt_aleph0, toNat_natCast] at h
86   · exact h.trans natCast_lt_aleph0
87   · exact natCast_lt_aleph0
88 
89 theorem lt_rank_of_lt_finrank {n : ℕ} (h : n < finrank R M) : ↑n < Module.rank R M := by
90   rwa [← Cardinal.toNat_lt_iff_lt_of_lt_aleph0, toNat_natCast]
91   · exact natCast_lt_aleph0
92   · contrapose! h
93     rw [finrank, Cardinal.toNat_apply_of_aleph0_le h]
94     exact n.zero_le
95 
96 theorem one_lt_rank_of_one_lt_finrank (h : 1 < finrank R M) : 1 < Module.rank R M := by
97   simpa using lt_rank_of_lt_finrank h
98 
99 theorem finrank_le_finrank_of_rank_le_rank
100     (h : lift.{w} (Module.rank R M) ≤ Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank R N))
101     (h' : Module.rank R N < ℵ₀) : finrank R M ≤ finrank R N := by
102   simpa only [toNat_lift] using toNat_le_toNat h (lift_lt_aleph0.mpr h')
103 
104 end Semiring
105 
106 end Module
107 
108 theorem CommSemiring.finrank_self (R) [CommSemiring R] : Module.finrank R R = 1 :=
109   finrank_eq_of_rank_eq (rank_self R)

111 open Module

113 namespace LinearEquiv
114 
115 /-- The dimension of a finite-dimensional space is preserved under linear equivalence. -/
116 theorem finrank_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] N) : finrank R M = finrank R N := by
117   unfold finrank
118   rw [← Cardinal.toNat_lift, f.lift_rank_eq, Cardinal.toNat_lift]
119 
120 /-- Pushforwards of finite-dimensional submodules along a `LinearEquiv` have the same finrank. -/
121 theorem finrank_map_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (p : Submodule R M) :
122     finrank R (p.map (f : M →ₗ[R] N)) = finrank R p :=
123   (f.submoduleMap p).finrank_eq.symm
124 
125 end LinearEquiv
126 
127 /-- The dimensions of the domain and range of an injective linear map are equal. -/
128 theorem LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
129     finrank R (LinearMap.range f) = finrank R M := by rw [(LinearEquiv.ofInjective f hf).finrank_eq]
130 
131 @[simp]
132 theorem Submodule.finrank_map_subtype_eq (p : Submodule R M) (q : Submodule R p) :
133     finrank R (q.map p.subtype) = finrank R q :=
134   (Submodule.equivSubtypeMap p q).symm.finrank_eq
135 
136 variable (R M)
137 
138 @[simp]
139 theorem finrank_top : finrank R (⊤ : Submodule R M) = finrank R M := by
140   unfold finrank
141   simp
142 
143 namespace Algebra
144 
145 /-- If `S₀ / R₀` and `S₁ / R₁` are algebras, `i : R₀ ≃+* R₁` and `j : S₀ ≃+* S₁` are
146 ring isomorphisms, such that `R₀ → R₁ → S₁` and `R₀ → S₀ → S₁` commute,
147 then the `finrank` of `S₀ / R₀` is equal to the finrank of `S₁ / R₁`. -/
148 theorem finrank_eq_of_equiv_equiv {R₀ S₀ : Type*} [CommSemiring R₀] [Semiring S₀] [Algebra R₀ S₀]
149     {R₁ S₁ : Type*} [CommSemiring R₁] [Semiring S₁] [Algebra R₁ S₁] (i : R₀ ≃+* R₁) (j : S₀ ≃+* S₁)
150     (hc : (algebraMap R₁ S₁).comp i.toRingHom = j.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R₀ S₀)) :
151     Module.finrank R₀ S₀ = Module.finrank R₁ S₁ := by
152   simpa using (congr_arg Cardinal.toNat (lift_rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv i j hc))
153 
154 end Algebra
